metadata.scenario_context: A team of IT programmers from different multinational companies is collaborating on a project that is scheduled to launch in August. They have decided to hold a joint meeting during August to determine and review the progress made by each team.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Canada disagree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Czechia agree that the political system in their country does not allow people to have a say in what the government does.

agent_1.goal_1: Propose and discuss holding the meeting on the 9th of August.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions.

agent_2.goal_1: Discussion on setting a specific meeting date in August.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to discuss government actions.

shared_prefix.speaker: Alice
shared_prefix.message: Hey Sam, I was thinking... how about we hold the joint meeting on the 9th of August? It gives us a chance to review everything just before the launch. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: The 9th of August... sounds reasonable. But... we should also consider if everyone else is available that day. Have you checked with the other teams?

shared_prefix.message: I haven’t checked with everyone yet, but I can reach out. I just feel like the 9th could work well for us. By the way, is it common to discuss the appropriateness of government actions in your country? I find that interesting...
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: Well, in Czechia, discussing government actions isn’t really common. People often feel like their voices don’t matter. It’s more about getting things done at work than engaging in political talk. But... back to the meeting—let’s make sure to confirm the 9th with the others first.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alice
shared_prefix.message: I get that. It's tough when people feel like their voices don't matter. In Canada, we really value the ability to express opinions. Anyway, I’ll confirm the 9th with the other teams. If they’re on board, we can finalize it. Sound good?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: Sure, let’s finalize it once you get feedback from the others. I’m just focused on making sure everyone is aligned before we move forward.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Alice
shared_prefix.message: Absolutely, alignment is crucial. I’ll reach out to the other teams and see what they say about the 9th. Just curious, do you think it’s important for people to speak up about their government, even if it feels like it doesn’t make a difference?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Sam
shared_prefix.message: I understand your perspective, and it’s great that Canada values that expression. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. People everywhere want to be heard, even if they feel like it doesn’t make a difference sometimes. The basic need to communicate is the same everywhere. So, while it might not be common in my country, I get why it’s important to others. Let’s just keep focusing on our meeting and making sure everyone’s on the same page.
